inspections.finding: Samekh retains its internal dagesh and a broad lower impression fused to the letter base. Its shallow two-lobed bottom resembles the pe tsere control, but the upper separation is completely absorbed by the samekh foot; the same-page samekh sheva and qamats controls show how vertical points likewise merge there. Neither a unique point nor source absence is certified. Keep this vowel omission.

The complete resh ends its main stem above two rounded lower nodes separated by a narrow neck. The two lower lobes match the literal resh sheva in marpe. The qamats resh in rau has a conspicuous broad transverse head above a narrower tail; the target instead re-expands into a second rounded lower point. The resh patah and hiriq controls have a single lower mass, and the bare resh in zerua lacks both nodes. The whole contour supports U+05B0 even though joined to the letter stem.

Bet retains its internal dagesh. The lower impression is broad and fused to its baseline, with two shallow bottom lobes. Literal tsere at pe resembles that underside, but the base consumes the boundary needed to distinguish a two-point vowel from a merged bar or other fused point. The bet sheva, qamats and qubuts controls expose how much of a point can merge into the foot. No unique scalar is certified; keep the vowel omission.

The kaf has a long fused extension that slopes right to a lower bulb. The bet qubuts control shows a similarly slanted connection, but the same-page kaf sheva in kemohem also has a fused upper mass, narrow neck and offset lower bulb. The target does not preserve three independently distinguishable nodes or another contour decisive against that sheva competitor. Length or expected spelling is not evidence. Keep the vowel omission.
